name: pigeonpea
sowing_season: Kharif: June–July with the monsoon, often intercropped with soybean, cotton, moong or jowar
soil: Well-drained loam to black soil, pH 6.5–7.5; very sensitive to waterlogging

stages.name: Germination / Emergence
stages.description: Seeds sprout and seedlings come up.
stages.irrigation: Sow after 75–100 mm of monsoon rain. Drain water quickly — standing water kills seedlings.
stages.fertilizer: Basal: 50 kg DAP per acre (add 8 kg sulphur if needed). Treat seed with Trichoderma 4 g + Carbendazim 1 g per kg, then Rhizobium + PSB 5 g per kg.
watch_for: Seedling rot and blight in waterlogged patches
tips: Seed rate 5–6 kg per acre as a sole crop; rows 60–90 cm apart
Sow on ridges or broad beds in heavy soil

stages.name: Early Vegetative
stages.description: Slow early growth; weeds can take over.
tips: Weed or hoe at 20–25 and 40–45 days
Intercrop rows of soybean, moong or jowar use the empty space in the early months

stages.name: Vegetative Growth
stages.description: Plants grow tall and branch out.
stages.irrigation: Rain-fed; give one protective irrigation in a long dry spell.
watch_for: Sterility mosaic — light green, bushy plants without flowers (spread by mites)
tips: Nip the top bud at 45–50 days for more branches
Uproot and destroy sterility mosaic plants early

stages.name: Flowering
stages.description: Yellow flowers open; most pod borer damage starts now.
stages.irrigation: Give one irrigation at flowering if the soil is dry.
watch_for: Maruca — flowers and pods webbed together
tips: Put up 5 pheromone traps and 20 bird perches per acre
Shake plants over a sheet to collect and destroy caterpillars

stages.name: Pod Formation / Pod Filling
stages.irrigation: A second protective irrigation at pod filling if it is dry.
watch_for: Pod fly — pods look healthy but the seeds inside are eaten
tips: Spray Emamectin benzoate 5 SG 0.4 g/litre at 50% flowering and again after 15 days if pod borer is seen
Neem seed kernel extract (5%) on young caterpillars

stages.name: Maturity / Harvest
tips: Harvest when 75–80% of pods are brown
Dry the grain well before storage

common_pests.name: Pod borer
common_pests.symptoms: Round holes in pods; caterpillars feeding on flowers and seeds
common_pests.control: Emamectin benzoate 5 SG 0.4 g/litre or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC 0.3 ml/litre

common_pests.name: Maruca pod borer
common_pests.symptoms: Flowers and pods webbed together with caterpillars inside

common_pests.name: Pod fly
common_pests.symptoms: Pods look healthy but the seeds inside are eaten; small exit holes
common_pests.control: Spray at pod formation; grow tolerant varieties

common_diseases.name: Fusarium wilt
common_diseases.symptoms: Plants wilt and dry in patches at flowering; brown-black band inside the stem
common_diseases.control: Resistant varieties, Trichoderma seed treatment, 3-year rotation, intercropping with jowar

common_diseases.name: Sterility mosaic
common_diseases.symptoms: Light green, bushy plants with small leaves and no flowers or pods
common_diseases.control: Uproot affected plants early; control the mites with wettable sulphur 80 WP 3 g/litre; resistant varieties

common_diseases.name: Phytophthora blight
common_diseases.symptoms: Water-soaked brown patches on the stem near the soil; plants break and dry
common_diseases.control: Good drainage and ridge sowing; seed treatment with Metalaxyl 35 SD 3 g per kg in problem fields
